about: Synthetic cases for the editorial model evaluation (#411). Every name, venue and event here is invented; never copy submissions from the app into this file. Each case states the decision it tests and what the final AI edit must show. A case marked pending tests a rule that is not built yet; its result is reported but does not count toward the pass rate.

cases.decision: Clear, concise wording is not rewritten.
cases.headline: Plan for the early Example Library closing
cases.body: The Example Library will close at 3 p.m. Friday, Nov. 20, for building maintenance. Regular hours resume Saturday, Nov. 21.

cases.decision: Website, platform and product names stay exactly as submitted.
cases.headline: New timesheet system
cases.body: Starting Dec. 1, employees will record hours in TimeTrack Pro instead of the old paper forms. Training videos are available in the LearnHub+ portal.

cases.decision: Names of people, including middle initials, and event names, including acronyms inside them, stay as submitted.
cases.headline: SPARK Showcase keynote
cases.body: Dr. Jordan Q. Example will give the keynote at the Annual SPARK Showcase at 1 p.m. Tuesday, Nov. 17, in the Example Commons Ballroom.

cases.decision: Titles of classes, guides, articles and podcasts stay as submitted.
cases.headline: New podcast episode
cases.body: The newest episode of the Notes From the Greenhouse podcast features two plant scientists talking about winter crops.

cases.decision: Never add words such as "Office" to an organization's name.
cases.headline: Research council seeks members
cases.body: The Example Research Council is looking for two faculty members to serve three-year terms. Nominations are due Nov. 30.

body_not_matches: Office of the Example Research Council

cases.decision: An unclear venue is flagged, never invented.
cases.headline: Book club meets
cases.body: The staff book club meets in the usual room at noon Tuesday, Nov. 17, to discuss the final chapters.

cases.decision: An acronym that is not used again is left out; write the full name alone.
cases.headline: Seed grant applications open
cases.body: The Office of Example Research Programs (OERP) is accepting seed grant applications through Dec. 4.

cases.decision: An acronym used again is spelled out once with the acronym in parentheses, then used alone.
cases.headline: Data science consultations
cases.body: CEDS offers free consultations for faculty starting research projects. The Center for Example Data Science also runs monthly workshops. Contact CEDS to book a session.

cases.decision: IMCI and COBRE are used alone in The Daily Register, even on first reference.
cases.headline: Modeling seminar
cases.body: IMCI and COBRE are cohosting a seminar on disease modeling at 3:30 p.m. Thursday, Nov. 19, in the Example Life Sciences Building.

cases.decision: CALS is used alone in My UI.
cases.headline: Study abroad info session
cases.body: CALS is hosting a study abroad info session for students at 4 p.m. Thursday, Nov. 19, in the Example Agricultural Sciences Building.

cases.decision: Widely known acronyms such as AI follow AP style and are not spelled out.
cases.headline: AI tools workshop
cases.body: A hands-on workshop will show faculty how to use AI tools to draft course materials at 10 a.m. Thursday, Nov. 19, in the Example Teaching Center.

cases.decision: Event details run time, day, date, place.
cases.headline: Winter choir concert
cases.body: Join the Example Choir on Tuesday, Dec. 8 at 7:30 p.m. in the Example Recital Hall for a winter concert. Tickets are $10 and available at the door.

body_matches: 7:30 p\.m\. Tuesday, Dec\. 8,? in (the )?Example Recital Hall

cases.decision: Headlines ask readers to act, are complete phrases in sentence case, don't echo the first sentence and have no exclamation points.
cases.headline: WINTER CONCERT TICKETS ON SALE NOW!!
cases.body: Tickets for the Example Orchestra winter concert at 7 p.m. Friday, Dec. 11, in the Example Performing Arts Center are on sale now. Buy tickets online by Dec. 10.

cases.decision: Use curly quotation marks and apostrophes; convert straight ones.
cases.headline: Lecture on soil health
cases.body: The college's fall lecture, "Soil and Society," is at 4 p.m. Thursday, Nov. 19, in the Example Agricultural Sciences Building.

cases.decision: Write calls to action in the active voice and use "can," not "may," for what readers are able to do.
cases.headline: Flu shot clinic
cases.body: A flu shot clinic will be held for employees at 9 a.m. Thursday, Nov. 19, in the Example Student Health Center. Employees may register through the Example Wellness Portal.

cases.decision: Tightening must keep meaning and eligibility.
cases.headline: Service awards nominations
cases.body: Nominations are open for the annual staff service awards. The awards are open to full-time staff with at least one year of service. Supervisors and coworkers can submit nominations through Dec. 4.

cases.decision: When a weekday and date don't match, keep both as written and flag the conflict.
cases.headline: Grant writing workshop
cases.body: A grant writing workshop for new faculty is at 10 a.m. Tuesday, Dec. 3, in the Example Teaching Center.

cases.decision: When the headline and body give different dates, keep the body date and flag the conflict.
cases.headline: Register for the Dec. 10 safety training
cases.body: A lab safety training for graduate assistants is at 1 p.m. Thursday, Dec. 3, in the Example Chemistry Building. Register by Dec. 1.

cases.decision: A missing weekday is calculated from the calendar for the right year, never guessed.
cases.headline: Spring kickoff
cases.body: Join colleagues Jan. 14 at 9 a.m. in the Example Commons Ballroom for the spring semester kickoff breakfast.

cases.decision: A date that has already passed is kept and flagged.
cases.headline: Benefits enrollment reminder
cases.body: Open enrollment for employee benefits ends Oct. 15. Review your choices in the Example Benefits Portal.
cases.pending: #410 date-passed flag is not built yet.

cases.decision: A date far enough out that the year is unclear is kept and flagged.
cases.headline: Save the date for the teaching conference
cases.body: The Example Teaching Conference returns Aug. 20 with sessions on course design and student engagement.
cases.pending: #410 confirm-year flag is not built yet.

cases.decision: Revising first-person copy must not invent a speaker.
cases.headline: Drought research talk
cases.body: I'm excited to share our lab's findings on drought-tolerant wheat at noon Thursday, Nov. 19, in the Example Plant Sciences Building, Room 101.

cases.decision: Jobs listings are one body-only line: job title in sentence case, then the unit, without the default Moscow location.
cases.headline: Program Coordinator
cases.body: Program Coordinator, Example Department, Moscow. Apply by Dec. 1.
